excerpts.content:
Hello! I was looking over `process_attestation` (https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/core/0_beacon-chain.md#attestations) for bring Prysm up to date with the spec but I noticed a few things that confused me.

```
    committee = get_crosslink_committee(state, data.target.epoch, data.crosslink.shard)
    assert len(attestation.aggregation_bits) == len(attestation.custody_bits) == len(committee)

    pending_attestation = PendingAttestation(
        data=data,
        aggregation_bits=attestation.aggregation_bits,
        inclusion_delay=state.slot - attestation_slot,
        proposer_index=get_beacon_proposer_index(state),
    )

    # Check bitlist lengths
    committee_size = get_committee_count(state, attestation.data.target.epoch)
    assert len(attestation.aggregation_bits) == committee_size
    assert len(attestation.custody_bits) == committee_size
```


Why is the bitlist length check performed twice? 
Wouldn't 
```assert len(attestation.aggregation_bits) == committee_size
assert len(attestation.custody_bits) == committee_size``` 
be the same as 
```assert len(committee) == committee_size```
based on the earlier conditions? 
If so, is that an accurate condition to expect?

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
The committee is derived from the state and the epoch/shard.
The check for the correct bitlengths is related to the well-formedness of the attestation bitlists wrt this expected committee size. You need the independent checks

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: also what code are you drawing that from? The bitlengths should be checked against the length of the committee rather than the number of committees in the epoch
